title: The electronics ‘under the hood’ of space networking
summary: SpaceNews interviews Jeff Janicik, founder and chairman of Innoflight, about space networking electronics, Golden Dome, Artemis, and collaborations with the Space Development Agency.

title: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth Partner to Connect Space and Soil
summary: LatConnect 60 and Phi Earth have partnered to integrate satellite and ground-based environmental data for nature-based projects. The collaboration aims to bridge the gap between orbital observations and field measurements.

title: RTX’s Blue Canyon Technologies introduces new spacecraft mission enabler
summary: Blue Canyon Technologies, a subsidiary of RTX, has introduced a new spacecraft subsystem aimed at enhancing mission capabilities for small satellites. This innovation is part of RTX's broader efforts to advance space technology and services.

title: The threat environment and processing at the edge
summary: SpaceNews interviews FrontGrade CTO Lorne Graves about how spacecraft processing power is adapting to megaconstellations and the benefits of satellite edge processing.

title: Propulsion is having a moment
summary: The article highlights the growing importance of propulsion in the space industry, featuring an interview with Kevin Lausten, CEO of Morpheus Space, at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference in Salt Lake City.

title: Space Angel secures $1.75m WA Government backing to advance Western Australian spaceport plans
summary: Space Angel received a $1.75 million grant from the Western Australian Government to advance plans for a spaceport. The funding was announced by Science and Innovation Minister Stephen Dawson.

title: Tendeg Launches NewTEN Steerable Compact Antenna at SmallSat
summary: Tendeg unveiled NewTEN, a two-axis steerable compact antenna designed to enhance communications for small spacecraft, at the SmallSat event in Salt Lake City. The innovation aims to improve pointing access and performance in space communications.

title: Robotics and the future of on-orbit labor
summary: SpaceNews interviews Icarus Robotics CEO Ethan Barajas at the 2026 Small Satellite Conference about the role of robotics in future on-orbit labor. The discussion highlights advancements in space robotics and their implications for space missions.

title: Spirit Electronics Adds Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology Space Grade Components to Online Store Ahead of SmallSat 2026
summary: Spirit Electronics expanded its online store to include space-grade components from Texas Instruments and Microchip Technology ahead of SmallSat 2026. This move supports the growing demand for high-reliability electronics in the space industry.

title: The Fuel for the Next Generation of Cislunar Exploration? Technology and Talent.
summary: The article discusses the future of cislunar exploration, highlighting the importance of technology and talent for upcoming missions. It reflects on past achievements like the Apollo moon landing and their long-term impacts.

title: Our choice as one of the best budget telescopes now has 17% off — this telescope deal is worth grabbing fast
summary: The Celestron StarSense Explorer DX 130AZ telescope, praised by an expert tester, is currently available at a 17% discount in a limited-time Amazon deal.

title: 'It's going to be beautiful': President Trump signs order to create US Space Academy
summary: President Trump signed an executive order to establish the U.S. Space Academy, aimed at training students for careers in space exploration, exploitation, and protection.

title: Relive private Chinese rocket's explosive 1st landing attempt (video)
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket's first landing attempt was explosive and captured on video. The footage highlights the dramatic nature of the failed landing test.

title: On Cloud 9: Have astronomers discovered the first starless galaxy?
summary: Astronomers may have discovered the first starless galaxy, which contains dark matter and gas but lacks stars. This finding could reshape understanding of galaxy formation.

title: SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket launching NASA's Roman Space Telescope on Aug. 30: How to watch it live
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is set to launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket on August 30. Live coverage details for the event have been provided.

title: On this day in space! Aug. 28, 1993: Galileo spacecraft flies by asteroid Ida on the way to Jupiter only to find a tiny moon!
summary: NASA's Galileo spacecraft discovered a tiny moon orbiting asteroid Ida during its flyby on Aug. 28, 1993, on its journey to Jupiter. This was a significant scientific finding as it was the first confirmed moon orbiting an asteroid.

title: Curiosity climbs to new heights on Mars | Space photo of the day for Aug. 28, 2026
summary: NASA's Curiosity Mars rover captured a new panorama after climbing a total of 1 kilometer on Mars during its 14-year exploration. The milestone highlights the rover's continued scientific contributions on the Red Planet.

title: President Trump gives Artemis II moon astronauts the Congressional Space Medal of Honor
summary: President Trump awarded the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the Artemis II moon astronauts who completed a lunar flyby mission in April. This marks a significant recognition for their historic achievement.

title: Soyuz MS-28 departs the ISS, three spacewalks install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae
summary: The Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft departed from the International Space Station. Three spacewalks were conducted to install upgrades to solar arrays and antennae.

title: Starbase, Louisiana: The Largest Private Spaceport in the World
summary: SpaceX has announced plans to develop 'Starbase, Louisiana,' which will be the largest private spaceport in the world. The initiative aims to expand SpaceX's launch capabilities and infrastructure.

title: Starbase’s future production capacity ramping up
summary: Starbase's production capacity is increasing due to heightened activity at the site. This expansion is likely aimed at supporting future spaceflight missions.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon Heavy to launch Roman telescope, Falcon 9 to launch Starlink satellites
summary: This week will feature five orbital launches, including a Falcon Heavy mission to deploy the Roman Space Telescope and a Falcon 9 launch carrying Starlink satellites. The launches will take place from China, the United States, and French Guiana.

title: NASA’s Roman telescope nears launch, reaches final integration and rehearsal milestones
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is nearing its launch, scheduled for August 30, after reaching final integration and rehearsal milestones.

title: LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 topples following milestone landing
summary: LandSpace's Zhuque-3 rocket achieved a significant milestone with a successful landing after its first stage flight. However, the rocket toppled over shortly after.

title: Ship 41 Completes Engine Testing Ahead of Flight 14
summary: Ship 41 has completed engine testing in preparation for Flight 14. Meanwhile, Ship 40 is being transported back to Starbase from Christmas Island.

title: Stoke Space conducts second stage fit checks, completes first stage engines ahead of Nova debut
summary: Stoke Space has completed second stage fit checks and finished first stage engines for its Nova rocket, aiming for a debut launch around 2026. This development highlights progress in reusable launch vehicle technology amid competition from SpaceX's Starship.

title: Zhuque-3 Completes Second Flight with Successful First-Stage Landing
summary: Zhuque-3, a methalox rocket developed by LandSpace, successfully completed its second flight and achieved a first-stage landing. This milestone marks a significant advancement for the company's reusable rocket technology.

title: Ship 40 arrives at Christmas Island, Plans Return to Starbase
summary: SpaceX has successfully guided Starship Ship 40 to a location near Christmas Island. The company plans to return the ship to its Starbase facility.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) has released a booklet highlighting 50 significant achievements over the past 50 years. This publication commemorates ESA's milestones and contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Phoenix 3: concept study for a reusable European spacecraft
summary: Engineers from ESA and industry partners completed a concept study for Phoenix 3, a reusable spacecraft for microgravity experiments and Earth return.

title: Proba-3’s eclipse hours before totality in Europe
summary: Proba-3, a mission by the European Space Agency, will create an artificial solar eclipse to study the Sun's corona just hours before the total solar eclipse in Europe. The mission aims to observe the Sun's outer atmosphere with unprecedented precision.

title: A double eclipse for Proba-3
summary: Proba-3 will experience a double eclipse as the Moon crosses its field of view. This event highlights the satellite's precise orbital alignment.

title: How ESA mimics and models the 2026 total solar eclipse
summary: ESA is preparing to study the 2026 total solar eclipse by using artificial eclipse missions and computer simulations to observe the Sun's corona. This effort is crucial for advancing solar science despite the rarity and brevity of natural eclipses.

title: Your chance to run software in deep space on ESA's asteroid mission
summary: The European Space Agency is inviting European researchers and companies to run their software aboard the Hera mission, a deep space asteroid mission. This offers a unique opportunity to test software in a deep space environment millions of kilometers away.

title: From drone flight to sounding rocket
summary: A student-developed radar retroreflector technology was tested for the first time during a drone flight at ESA's ESTEC technical centre in the Netherlands. The payload was carried by a drone, marking a transition from drone flight to sounding rocket applications.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use a coronagraph to study the Sun by blocking its light, simulating an eclipse. The mission involves two satellites playing a 'hide and seek' game to position the coronagraph correctly.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event will showcase innovative space startups and facilitate collaboration with Europe's space industry on September 16-17 at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands.

title: Launch Concerns Cast a Shadow Over SmallSat 2026
summary: The space industry faces potential launch challenges for SmallSat 2026 if current launch market conditions do not improve. Without changes, rapid growth could lead to significant setbacks.

title: ICEYE Opens Three International Offices in a Single Week
summary: ICEYE expanded its global presence by opening three international offices in a single week. This rapid expansion highlights the company's growth in the space industry.

title: Canadian Companies Partner on SDA Sat Solution
summary: Canadian companies are collaborating on a Space Development Agency (SDA) satellite solution. This development coincides with SpaceX offering free access to its Space Situational Awareness (SSA) catalog for smallsat operators and LeoLabs preparing to demonstrate its SDA capabilities for U.S. national-security missions.

title: Space Weather Losses to Double by 2035, Report Finds
summary: A new report from Mission Space predicts that solar storms will cause $20.65 billion in losses in 2026, increasing to $44.27 billion by 2035. The findings highlight the growing economic impact of space weather on industries reliant on satellite and ground-based technologies.

title: LeoLabs Wins $20.68M Space Force Award for Scout
summary: LeoLabs secured a $20.68 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to deploy its radar technology for national security missions. The award highlights the growing role of commercial space surveillance in supporting defense operations.

title: SpaceX Announces New Starbase, Louisiana Spaceport
summary: SpaceX announced a new high-cadence launch site in Louisiana for future Starship operations, with Gwynne Shotwell and Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry present at the announcement.

title: Exclusive: City Labs Plans Second Nuclear Demo
summary: City Labs is planning a second nuclear demonstration following the success of its first nuclear-powered betavoltaic demo. The upcoming demo will focus on a radioisotope heating unit.

title: White House Wants 1,000 Annual Launches and Reentries by 2030
summary: The White House has set a goal of achieving 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030 through a new National Space Transportation Policy, replacing the 2013 edition. This policy aims to significantly expand U.S. space transportation capabilities.

title: The Aerospace Corp’s Disksat Gains Commercial Traction
summary: The Aerospace Corporation's DiskSat, a unique box-less satellite design, is gaining commercial traction. This innovative configuration is proving to be a successful approach for the company.

title: Exclusive: OrbitAID to Launch RPO Demo in 2027
summary: OrbitAID plans to launch a rendezvous and proximity operations (RPO) demonstration in 2027, aiming to validate the entire satellite life extension process in a single mission. Unlike previous demonstrations, this mission will integrate far-range inspection and close-approach maneuvering.

title: Smaller Space Companies Want to See Programs of Record for Their Investments
summary: Smaller space companies are seeking clarity on how the Pentagon's 'commercial first' acquisition policy will be implemented through formal programs of record. The Space Force has introduced nine new program acquisitions to address this demand.

title: India’s InspeCity Raises $10.5M in Pre-Series A round
summary: India’s InspeCity, a space startup, raised $10.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round to fund four upcoming on-orbit missions over the next 18 months.

title: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope Set for Falcon Heavy Launch on Sunday
summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is scheduled to launch on Sunday aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The mission honors the legacy of NASA's first chief of astronomy.

title: Europe’s Meteosat Third Generation Constellation Complete After Latest Launch
summary: Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) constellation is now complete after the latest launch by Arianespace on Aug. 27. The system's imaging capabilities are confirmed operational by EUMETSAT.

title: Ovzon to Enter German Market With New Partnerships
summary: Swedish satellite operator Ovzon is entering the German market through two new partnerships. The company will conduct an initial test implementation with a German government entity.

title: PLD Space, Isar Aerospace, and Rocket Factory Augsburg Land ESA Contracts in Launch Challenge
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) awarded over 500 million euros to PLD Space, Isar Aerospace, and Rocket Factory Augsburg for the European Launch Challenge. This funding supports the development of new launch capabilities in Europe.

title: Astrum Space Strikes SPAC Deal for D2D Service at $1B Valuation
summary: Astrum Space has agreed to a SPAC deal to go public at a $1 billion valuation, aiming to fund its satellite-to-device broadcast network for the Asia-Pacific region.

title: Lite Coms Adds SES MEO Compatibility, Comtech WGS-Certified Modem to Lite Sat 1.3A Terminal
summary: Lite Coms has added SES MEO compatibility and a Comtech WGS-certified modem to its Lite Sat 1.3A terminal. The terminal is now available for SES O3b mPOWER Sovereign Services and Hybrid Sovereign Gateway architectures.

title: Kepler Enters Optical Tech Partnership, Hosted Payload Agreement with NorthStar
summary: Kepler Communications has partnered with NorthStar to integrate its optical data relay infrastructure with NorthStar's Space Domain Awareness services. The strategic agreement aims to enhance space-based data transmission and monitoring capabilities.

title: LeoLabs to Provide Space Force With Surveillance Radar
summary: LeoLabs secured a $20.7 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to deliver a modified Scout space surveillance radar. The deal involves providing a containerized radar system for space domain awareness.
